FAST · ON-DEVICE AI The wind howled like a dying beast against the iron ribs of the tower, rattling the brass fittings until they groaned in protest. Elias stared out at the churning grey sea, his face illuminated only by the flickering blue light that pierced the dark water. He had been here for four years, guarding this very lighthouse with a single eye and a heart too big for the world outside it. For weeks, the weather had been a relentless gauntlet. The gale force ten storms battered the structure, sending splinters of wood flying and threatening to topple the lantern room. Yet, Elias remained. He was a keeper of light in an age that had forgotten what it meant to look upward with hope. The ship's crew had been gone for months after the storm. The captain was presumed dead, leaving only this solitary figure against the encroaching darkness. There were no other voices on the tower; not even the faint sound of a dog barking or the chirping of birds. It was an eerie silence that pressed against his ears, but Elias did not complain. His duty was to maintain the beam until dawn broke and the world returned to normalcy. He took a deep breath, filling his lungs with the salty air. The oil lamp on his desk had been burning steadily for hours now, casting a warm pool of light onto the worn wooden floorboards. Shadows danced across the walls as he moved slowly toward the main window, checking the glass for cracks or damage that might affect the beam's strength. He knew the routine better than anyone else in the world; it was the only thread connecting him to the community and to the trust placed on his shoulders. He adjusted the crank of the Fresnel lens with a steady hand, ensuring there were no gaps where darkness could slip through. This was not just maintenance; it was an act of defiance against the chaos outside. While other people might have sought shelter from the storm in their cars or homes, Elias chose to stand as a beacon of stability, a silent promise that help would come if they needed it most. The sun began to crest over the horizon, painting the sky in hues of gold and orange before fading back into twilight blue. The gale had passed, but the air still carried the smell of salt and ozone from hours ago. Elias extinguished the lamp slowly, letting the darkness swallow him whole once more. He walked down the stairs, leaving his gear on the table, ready to wait for the next ship that might arrive to fill the void left by the departed crew. The tower stood tall, a silent sentinel watching over the ocean, its purpose clear and unchanging even when the world around it seemed broken. Ledger
